problem:
A body of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}$ meters per second.
Find an expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-{t}^{2}) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =6\cdot (3{t}^{2}-2t) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-12t.\end{aligned}
$$
